messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — planning a Terraform change to add a new GPU node pool for model-training workloads. Goal: 24/7 reserved baseline + spot for burst. Will paste the TF snippet and a k8s node pool manifest for review. Ping if you see any risky bits.

ben: sg, what's the target instance family? p3, p4, a100, or cheaper 40gb?

maya: Thinking rtx6000-equivalent for dev (g4dn.12x) and p4d for heavy training batches. We want 2 reserved vms always (capacity reservation) and an autoscaled spot group up to 8.

carol: +1 on reserved baseline. For p4d we should ensure AMI/ENI limits are ok. Also confirm EBS throughput.

jess: Can you share the TF snippet? also need the nodeSelector/taint plan so infra teams know pods won't land on these unless requested.

maya: Paste:```hcl
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_lt" {
  name_prefix   = "redwood-gpu-"
  image_id      = var.gpu_ami
  instance_type = var.gpu_instance_type
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

resource "aws_ec2_capacity_reservation" "gpu_cr" {
  capacity_reservation_specification {
    capacity_reservation_preference = "open"
  }
  instance_type = var.gpu_instance_type
  availability_zone = var.az
  instance_count = var.reserved_count
  tags = { Name = "redwood-gpu-reservation" }
}

module "eks_node_group_gpu" {
  source = "./modules/eks-gpu"
  launch_template_id = aws_launch_template.gpu_lt.id
  desired_capacity = var.desired_capacity
  max_capacity = var.max_capacity
  spot = var.use_spot
}
```

maya: k8s node pool plan:```yaml
apiVersion: eksctl.io/v1alpha5
kind: ClusterConfig
nodeGroups:
- name: gpu-reserved
  labels: { role: gpu, pool: reserved }
  taints:
  - key: gpu
    value: reserved
    effect: NoSchedule
  instanceType: p4d.24xlarge
  desiredCapacity: 2
  maxSize: 2
- name: gpu-spot
  labels: { role: gpu, pool: spot }
  taints:
  - key: gpu
    value: spot
    effect: NoSchedule
  instanceType: p4d.24xlarge
  desiredCapacity: 0
  maxSize: 8
  spot: true
```

maya: Secrets wiring: we'll keep SSH keys and AMI credentials in the vault (KMS-backed), TF reads via vault provider; kube bootstrap uses a pre-created k8s secret per-cluster: `kubectl create secret generic gpu-keys --from-literal=ami-creds=$(vault read -field=value secret/gpu/ami)`

dave: Quick question: capacity reservations in AWS are regional AZ-scoped — do we create one-per-az or stick to single-az reservation? Multi-az preferred for resilience.

maya: Plan is 2 reservations spread across 2 AZs (1 each) so reserved_count stays small but resilient. TF will loop over azs.

ben: If spot fails, what's fallback? auto-scaling should spin up on-demand nodes from the reserved LT? We need launch template override to prefer on-demand when spot capacity not available.

carol: In TF use mixed_instances_policy with overrides: set instance_market_options to spot for the spot group and leave reserved group as on-demand. Also add a fallback policy in kube cluster-autoscaler: `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false --balance-similar-node-groups` and set `--expander=least-waste` so it prefers reserved nodes.

jess: Also add a pod annotation for tolerations so only workloads with toleration land on GPU pools. Mention this in the docs.

maya: Good call. I'll add CI checks: ensure node group manifests include taints/labels and that any GPU workload has tolerations in manifests (scan via a simple grep in the deployment linter).

ops-ci: CI pipeline: gpu-nodepool-apply job queued — terraform plan failed on `aws_ec2_capacity_reservation` due to missing `ami` tag. See: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/3421 (bot) :warning:

maya: grabbing that now. likely the module expects `ami` var. will push a fix and re-run.

dave: One more: for cost accounting tag everything with `cost-center` + `team`. Also add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [tag] }` carefully if tags are managed elsewhere.

maya: Thanks — will update tags + add doc snippet in infra README about how to create the k8s secret and vault paths. I'll open a small PR in a bit; ping me in-thread for quick review. :thumbsup:
